- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.7) and forecast shows a sharp upward spike, reduce the peak by 5–10% to avoid overshoot.  
- If sentiment turns negative (≤ -0.3) and forecast is still trending up, shift forecast downward by 2–5% to align with sentiment reversal.  
- For 30-day horizons, if recent 5–7 day prices show strong mean reversion (e.g., 2–3 consecutive drops), model should not overcorrect upward; cap forecast at 1–2% above recent high.  
- If sentiment is neutral or mixed (±0.3) and forecast is consistently above true outcome, apply a 3–5% downward bias to avoid overconfidence.  
- When sentiment history shows a recent “pullback” (e.g., 2–3 negative sentiment days), forecast should not assume continuation of prior trend; adjust for lagged momentum.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome is consistently below forecast for 3+ consecutive days, apply a 2–4% downward correction to avoid overestimating future volatility.
